summary: Autonomous driving is the visible front, but AI runs through freight matching, maritime navigation, transit operations, and aviation. Who tracks it: the safety regulators and standards bodies are the primary record, with the operators' own published data layered on top.

analysis.body:
Per the Census Bureau, 13.0% of firms in transportation and warehousing (NAICS 48-49) answered Yes to whether they used AI in the last two weeks, up from 7.9% in the prior period. The question was first asked in September 2023. That is the only measured adoption figure in the material, and it sits well below the visibility of autonomy in this sector, which suggests the headline deployments are concentrated among large operators while the typical firm has not yet adopted.

What AI is deployed for in transportation, according to the sources, splits into driving and back-office functions. Aurora describes the Aurora Driver as self-driving freight technology backed by verifiable AI, integrated into fleets and into the Volvo VNL Autonomous, with a hybrid model pairing professional drivers with the driver on long-haul routes such as Fort Worth to El Paso. Waymo, which began as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009 and served its first fully autonomous rides in 2015, publishes a safety program for fully autonomous driving and supports the U.S. Department of Transportation National Roadway Safety Strategy through its ride-hailing service. C.H. Robinson applies AI to logistics orchestration, describing a supply chain that analyzes, decides, executes, and improves continuously across every shipment, and runs an AI assistant for shipping options. Samsara reports its connected operations platform serves 20,000+ operations with AI-driven alerts, predictive analytics, and dash cam safety technology, and states 380,000+ accidents prevented.

Vendors and money concentrate around a few named players. Aurora works with Werner and Volvo. Samsara sells fleet telematics at scale. Wärtsilä supplies marine and energy technology, including AI-driven predictive analytics for decarbonisation. Airbus frames its innovation work around a decarbonised, connected and autonomous future for aerospace. The American Trucking Associations represents more than 37,000 members through a federation of 50 state trucking associations, which is where autonomous freight policy is tracked. The site's own directory tracks Palantir as the enterprise AI platform used by airlines and rail operators for fleet and crew optimization, and catalogs robotics models, including vision-language-action models, from the Hugging Face Hub.

ROI evidence in the excerpts is mostly vendor-reported. Samsara's 380,000+ accidents prevented is the clearest quantified claim, tied to AI-powered dash cams, real-time in-cab alerts, and automated coaching. Aurora's customers describe safety and efficiency benefits and better driver lives from handing off lengthier, less desirable routes, and one cites freight volumes projected to grow five fold between 2010-2050 as making autonomous transport a necessity. C.H. Robinson frames its value as autonomous logistics orchestration rather than a cost figure. No source here reports a measured return in currency.

The regulatory posture is active and gatekeeping. EASA's Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 sets out its vision for safety and ethical considerations of AI in aviation, with an action plan, conceptual guidance, and anticipated rulemaking, amended once a year. The IMO adopted a new International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships in May 2026, effective 1 July 2026, a goal-based framework requiring a MASS Safety Certificate, covering operating conditions such as wind speed, sea state, visibility, water depth, and day versus night limits. The IMO notes there are currently no commercially operating, internationally trading SOLAS cargo ships that operate autonomously or remotely-controlled, though trials have shown feasibility. The site's own points add that the FAA's innovation work and EASA's roadmap are the regulatory record for AI flight systems and eVTOL certification, and that nothing flies commercially without them.

For a reader deciding whether to deploy, the material points to a sector where the technology is proven in trials and pilots but adoption is still thin at the firm level, and where the gating factors are certification regimes rather than model capability. The IMO's functional approach, assessing which ship functions are remote, autonomous, or crewed, is a template for that assessment. The sources do not report deployment costs, failure rates, or labor effects beyond driver-route anecdotes, so those questions remain open here.

https://www.samsara.com/.brief: Samsara claims its connected operations platform supports more than 20,000 operations in improving safety, cutting costs, and running smarter. The platform analyzes data to provide AI-driven alerts, predictive analytics, and actionable insights that help spot risks and optimize operations. According to Samsara, its AI-powered dash cams, real-time in-cab alerts, automated coaching, and other safety technologies have prevented over 380,000 accidents. The system includes cameras and video AI, multicam support, driver experience tools, driver coaching, drowsiness detection, safety reporting & insights, and equipment management.

https://www.trucking.org/.brief: ATA, the American Trucking Association, says it is the largest and most comprehensive national trade association for trucking. It reports that Miguel Corral, a UPS driver, was named Bendix Grand Champion at the 2026 National Truck Driving & Step Van Championships. ATA says it has more than 37,000 members, including carriers, suppliers, shippers, and professionals, and that it works to influence government policy, educate stakeholders, and host events that bring together all parts of the industry.

https://www.wartsila.com/.brief: Wärtsilä describes itself as a global leader in technologies and lifecycle solutions for the marine and energy markets. The company states that while no single solution will carry the transition, most of the technology needed to decarbonise already exists. It cites engines that run flexibly on low- and zero-carbon fuels and AI-driven predictive analytics among the tools it offers customers for their decarbonisation efforts. Wärtsilä also reports it will supply a 282 MW onsite power solution for a U.S. data center, which it links to AI growth intensifying demand for reliable power.

https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/domains/re.brief: The EASA has published an Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 that outlines the Agency's approach to safety and ethical considerations for AI in aviation. The roadmap provides an action plan for the EASA AI Programme, including conceptual guidance and anticipated rulemaking activities, and serves as a basis for stakeholder discussions. As a living document, it will be updated annually and refined through stakeholder exchanges and the Agency's ongoing practical work on AI development.

https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/HotTo.brief: The IMO introduced a new International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS Code) in May 2026, which became effective on 1 July 2026. A ship is considered a MASS only when autonomous or remote technologies replace or support crew functions and it holds a valid MASS Safety Certificate; enhanced automation alone does not qualify. The Code offers voluntary, technology-neutral guidance that complements existing regulations and defines operating conditions, limits, and responses when those limits are exceeded, creating a “goal-based framework” for safe design, operation, and certification. Trials under interim MSC 110 guidelines in June 2019 have shown that larger remotely controlled and autonomous ships are feasible, and while no SOLAS cargo ships are yet operating autonomously, the IMO anticipates commercial service in the near future with a gradual evolution toward more advanced MASS. An IMO seminar in April 2024 addressed the implications, challenges, and opportunities of MASS for ports and public authorities.

https://theworldofai.org/ai-ecosystem/te.brief: The page catalogues the 1000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, listing each model's licence, download count and release date, and is refreshed daily. It states that the data comes from the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads, with every model linking to its own Hub page. The page was last verified on 2026-10-06 and is described as free to read, cite and query. It also notes that the site's other pages are rebuilt daily from primary sources and carry their last-verified date.
